newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No limits on GBL stake - Suez.
newsitem.headline: No limits on GBL stake - Suez.

text.p: French holding company Compagnie de Suez said there were no limits on the equity stake which Belgian holding company Groupe Lambert Bruxelles (GBL), or for that matter other "friendly groups", could hold in Suez.

"I use this interview to correct something. I have never set any limits regarding the capital of Suez. Certainly not for friendly groups which have entered (the capital) in perfect harmony (with Suez)," Gerard Mestrallet, chief executive officer of Suez, told Belgian Trends magazine.
He said he had been misquoted by a Belgian newspaper which reported last month that a seven percent stake was the limit for individual shareholders.
The remark had been made in the context of GBL purchases of Suez shares amounting to five percent of Suez' capital.

Newspaper De Financieel Economische Tijd had said GBL could boost its stake in Suez to a maximium seven percent. Anything above that would make it a dominant shareholder, which was not acceptable to Suez.
A GBL unit bought 2.9 percent in Suez from Elf Aquitaine on October 7 and was reported on October 23 to have taken another one percent from French insurer UAP.
Since then GBL, led by reclusive Belgian financier Albert Frere, is said to have boosted its stake to five percent.
Suez shareholder UAP is a longtime ally of Frere. UAP and GBL together control Belgian insurer Royale Belge SA.
